universe.acceptedNote: Owner choice. No book prescribes these thresholds.

factors.name: Return on invested capital

definitions.taxRate: clamp(incomeTax_ttm / pretaxIncome_ttm, 0, maxTaxRate); defaultTaxRate when pretaxIncome_ttm <= 0 or missing

factors.acceptedNote: The book uses EBIT × (1 - tax) over total capital. The register nets cash and averages invested capital, as is common practice.

factors.name: Gross profitability
factors.formula: grossProfit_ttm / avg(totalAssets). If grossProfit is missing use revenue_ttm - costOfRevenue_ttm
factors.acceptedNote: No book in the knowledge base defines it.

factors.name: Free cash flow margin
factors.acceptedNote: Free cash flow follows Reilly & Brown page 315. No book defines the margin.

factors.name: Accruals
factors.acceptedNote: No book in the knowledge base defines it.

factors.name: Net debt to EBITDA
factors.formula: (longTermDebt + shortTermDebt - cash) / (operatingIncome_ttm + depreciationAmortization_ttm). None when the denominator is not positive
factors.acceptedNote: BKM page 497 lists total debt to EBITDA by rating class only. No book defines the net form.

factors.name: Interest coverage
factors.formula: operatingIncome_ttm / interestExpense_ttm, capped at coverageCap. Equals the cap when interest expense is zero or missing and debt is zero
factors.acceptedNote: The book uses EBIT. Operating income stands in for it, and the cap handles zero interest.

citation.document: BKM - Investment and Portfolio Management - Edition 9.pdf

factors.name: Earnings yield
factors.formula: operatingIncome_ttm / enterpriseValue, where enterpriseValue = marketCap + longTermDebt + shortTermDebt - cash. None when enterprise value is not positive
factors.acceptedNote: The book uses earnings per share over price. Operating income over enterprise value keeps firms with different debt comparable.

citation.quote: the ratio of the annual earnings to the market price

factors.name: Free cash flow yield
factors.acceptedNote: Graham & Dodd page 41 names free cash flow yield without a formula.

factors.name: Momentum 12-1
factors.acceptedNote: The books use the past 3 to 12 months. Skipping the latest month avoids short-term reversal, the standard academic construction.

citation.document: Lectures on Financial Economics, Antonio Mele.pdf
citation.quote: Stocks with the highest returns in the previous twelve months will outperform in the next future.

factors.name: Above the 200-session average
factors.acceptedNote: The book treats a cross up through the moving average as a bullish signal. The register scores how far the price is above the 200-session average.

citation.document: BKM - Investment and Portfolio Management - Edition 9.pdf
citation.quote: When the market price breaks through the moving average line from below, as at point A in Figure 12.5, it is taken as a bullish signal

factors.name: Volatility
factors.formula: Standard deviation of daily log returns over 252 sessions, times sqrt(252)
factors.acceptedNote: The book uses the sample standard deviation, dividing by N-1. The register divides by N. The annualisation factor is 252.

citation.quote: we needed the factor 252, supposing that there are approximately 252 business days in a year
some analysts only subtract capital expenditures, and those who are conservative also subtract dividends

composite.acceptedNote: Outliers are limited to ±3 standard deviations about the mean, as the book does. Within-sector z-scores and the group weights are an owner choice.

citation.quote: One rule of thumb is to pull in all outliers in the Xn,k(t) to ±3 standard deviations about the mean.

screen.acceptedNote: Owner choice. No book prescribes these thresholds.
